1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator entropy source configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a permutation or hash function circuit configured to receive and process at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to generate a second entropy value, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit is configured to apply countermeasures against phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator entropy source;
a pseudorandom number generator circuit seeded with the second entropy value; and
a cryptographic processing circuit configured to generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic processing circuit is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic processing circuit is configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a single ring oscillator.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to a permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit comprises a hash function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit comprises a bit-mixer.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to generate the second entropy value.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function circuit implements countermeasures comprising at least one of: jitter injection, phase randomization, or multi-oscillator mixing to prevent phase tracking attacks.

12. (Cancelled)

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator entropy source;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation or hash function configured with countermeasures against phase tracking attacks to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a single ring oscillator.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation or hash function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to a permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the permutation or hash function comprises a hash function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the permutation or hash function comprises a bit-mixer.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to generate the second entropy value.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the permutation or hash function implements countermeasures comprising at least one of: jitter injection, phase randomization, or multi-oscillator mixing to prevent phase tracking attacks.

24. (Cancelled)
